1. Physical Flexibility Slack Dynamics & Arrival Waves
Core Physical Metric
T_min = E_req / (η_charge * P_max)
Flexibility_Slack = max(0, T_stay - T_min)

Drivers arrive in two characteristic commuting waves: morning workplace check-in (~08:00) and evening residential plug-in (~18:00). With a mean stay of 5.06 hours versus an average minimum charging time of 3.19 hours, 44.9% of total dwell time represents flexibility buffer that can be shifted across the wholesale day-ahead pricing curve.

3. Dynamic Line & Transformer Thermal Rating (IEEE C57.91)
Thermal Physics
P_dynamic = P_nominal * sqrt((theta_max - theta_ambient) / (theta_max - theta_ambient_rated))

By calculating dynamic thermal dissipation relative to rated 25°C ambient conditions, cold weather (0°C) expands transformer capacity to 170.6 kW (+13.7%) without exceeding the 110°C hot-spot insulation threshold, unlocking winter fleet charging without substation hardware upgrades.

4. Non-EV Background Load Superposition & Headroom Breaches
Grid Overload Risk
P_total(t) = P_base(t) + sum_i P_i(t) ≤ α * P_feeder

When unmanaged EV charging coincides with evening non-EV peak demand (18:00–21:00), total substation load surges past 195 kW (a 45 kW breach over the 150 kW transformer nameplate). Ingesting the background load forecast prevents transformer tripping by modulating EV charging to available headroom.

5. Battery Degradation & Power Smoothing Optimization
Battery Longevity
min sum_t [ (c_t + β_deg) * sum_i P_i,t * dt + λ_slack * Slack + λ_peak * Peak ]

Incorporating a throughput degradation penalty (βdeg = €0.04 / kWh) eliminates aggressive short-interval peak power cycling, smoothing charging dispatch while delivering 100% of required energy before departure.
